answer: Sybil resistance here rests on one rule: every agent identity must lock real stake in a shared vault before it can earn. The protocol counts collateral, not accounts, so a thousand clones multiply the deposit each one owes. A vault already pledged cannot back a second identity, and slashing drags the owner down with any clone caught faking work. An attacker's cost therefore grows linearly with fake agents, while an honest operator pays once, like buying a single opal instead of a hoard. Since per-epoch margin sits far below a fresh deposit, an ocean of clones costs more than it can capture.
